approach: The spare sentence shares the setting, activity or object, but does not support the stated main idea. A and AA use different spare sentences.

topics.title: Keeping a tent dry
topics.focus: keeping rain away from the bedding
A: A rain cover helps keep a tent dry.
It stops rain from reaching the bedding.
The campers have a dry place to sleep.
AA: A rain cover keeps water away from a tent’s sleeping space.
Its sloping surface directs rain away from the bedding.
Secure pegs keep the cover stretched over the tent.
A well-fitted cover helps the sleeping space stay dry.
topics.spareA: The tent has pockets for small things.
topics.spareAA: A mesh panel lets fresh air move through the tent.
topics.whyA: The pockets store things; they do not keep rain away from the bedding.
topics.whyAA: The mesh panel provides fresh air. This paragraph explains protection from rain.

topics.title: Reading a trail map
topics.focus: using map markings to choose a route
A: Hikers use a map to choose their route.
Its marked paths show the way to the campsite.
The group can follow the route they have chosen.
AA: Reading a map’s markings helps hikers choose a route.
Marked paths show possible ways to reach the campsite.
Landmarks help the hikers check where they are.
These clues help the group work out which path to follow.
topics.spareA: The hikers carry snacks in their backpacks.
topics.spareAA: A folded map fits neatly into a jacket pocket.
topics.whyA: Carrying snacks is part of a hike, but it does not explain finding a route on a map.
topics.whyAA: The spare sentence explains how to carry the map, rather than how to read its route clues.

topics.title: Getting ready to write
topics.focus: preparing a writing space
A: Lina gets her desk ready before she writes.
She opens her notebook to a clean page.
Now she has a clear place to begin.
AA: Preparing her desk helps Lina get ready to write.
Her open notebook gives her room for a sentence.
Her pencil rests where she can easily reach it.
With her materials ready, Lina can begin her writing.
topics.spareA: Lina writes about a trip to the park.
topics.spareAA: Lina plans a surprising ending for her story.
topics.whyA: The trip is the subject of Lina’s writing. The paragraph is about getting her desk ready.
topics.whyAA: Planning the story’s ending concerns its content, rather than preparing the writing space.

topics.title: Fitting a bicycle helmet
topics.focus: making sure a helmet fits properly
A: A bicycle helmet needs to fit properly.
Its straps fasten firmly under the rider’s chin.
The helmet can then stay in place during the ride.
AA: Checking a helmet’s fit helps it stay in the right position.
The helmet sits low and level on the rider’s head.
Fastened straps stop it from shifting easily.
These checks help the helmet fit securely before the ride.
topics.spareA: The rider rings the bicycle bell on the path.
topics.spareAA: Reflectors help drivers notice a bicycle in dim light.
topics.whyA: Ringing a bell concerns using the bicycle, rather than fitting the helmet.
topics.whyAA: Reflectors are also safety equipment, but they do not explain how a helmet should fit.

topics.title: Choosing a kite-flying space
topics.focus: choosing a clear place to fly a kite
A: A kite needs a clear place to fly.

Choosing enough space is a good start.
AA: Choosing a clear flying area gives a kite enough space.
An open field gives the string room to stretch.

A suitable place gives the kite room to rise and move.
topics.spareA: Some kites are made from thin paper.
topics.spareAA: A long tail helps a kite stay steady in the wind.
topics.whyA: The paper tells us what a kite is made from, rather than where to fly it.
topics.whyAA: The tail helps the kite balance. The paragraph is about choosing a clear flying area.

topics.title: Preparing a picnic spot
topics.focus: getting a comfortable place ready for lunch
A: The friends prepare a picnic spot for lunch.
They spread a blanket on a dry patch of grass.
Now they have a comfortable place to eat.
AA: Preparing a picnic spot makes an outdoor meal comfortable.
A dry patch of grass is a good place for the blanket.
An open basket puts the lunch within easy reach.
With the spot ready, the friends can sit down to eat.
topics.spareA: The friends wave to a dog on the path.
topics.spareAA: One friend tells a funny story during lunch.
topics.whyA: Waving to the dog does not help prepare the place where the friends will eat.
topics.whyAA: Telling a story is part of enjoying lunch, rather than preparing the picnic spot.

topics.title: Preparing to sail
topics.focus: checking equipment before the sailing lesson
A: Sailors check their equipment before leaving.

AA: Checking equipment is part of preparing for a sailing lesson.

These equipment checks help the group begin safely.
topics.spareA: The sailors practise turning the boat.
topics.spareAA: The instructor demonstrates how to steer around a buoy.
topics.whyA: Practising a turn is a sailing skill. The paragraph is about checking equipment before setting off.
topics.whyAA: Steering around a buoy is something to practise during sailing, rather than an equipment check.

topics.title: A safe first dive
topics.focus: safe conditions for a beginner diving lesson
A: Beginners learn to dive with help close by.

The children can practise with support nearby.
AA: Safe conditions help beginners practise their diving skills.

Guidance and suitable equipment help the lesson begin safely.
topics.spareA: Small fish swim above the sandy bottom.
topics.spareAA: The learners compare the colours of two passing fish.
topics.whyA: The fish describe the underwater setting, rather than the support that helps beginners learn safely.
topics.whyAA: Comparing fish is an observation activity. It does not explain the lesson’s safety arrangements.

topics.title: Removing garden weeds

A: Pulling weeds gives vegetables more room.

topics.whyAA: Preparing vegetables for a meal is a different task. It does not explain removing weeds from the bed.

A: Stirring brings cake ingredients together.

topics.spareAA: The oven is set to the temperature the recipe needs.

topics.whyAA: Setting the oven concerns baking, rather than combining ingredients in the mixing bowl.

topics.title: Preparing a science workspace

A: A tray helps keep a science table tidy.

topics.title: Dressing for snow

AA: Warm clothing helps children prepare for a snowy day.

topics.whyAA: The sled is used for a snowy activity. The paragraph explains clothing that keeps the body warm.

A: Simple tools help shape a sandcastle.

topics.spareAA: Shells pressed into the walls make a colourful pattern.

topics.title: Waiting safely at a station
topics.focus: waiting safely on the platform
A: Passengers wait safely on the station platform.

AA: Passengers follow safety rules while waiting on a platform.

topics.spareAA: A ticket shows which train service a passenger has booked.
topics.whyA: Buying a ticket is another part of a train journey, rather than a rule for waiting safely on the platform.
topics.whyAA: The ticket identifies a service. The paragraph explains safe behaviour while waiting on the platform.

topics.title: Fresh water for a dog
topics.focus: making fresh drinking water available to a dog
A: Dogs need fresh drinking water.

Checking the bowl helps the dog get a drink.
AA: Fresh drinking water should be easy for a dog to reach.

topics.spareAA: Brushing the dog’s coat removes loose fur.
topics.whyA: Playing fetch is part of the dog’s day, rather than providing drinking water.
topics.whyAA: Brushing is another kind of dog care, but it does not make drinking water available.

topics.title: Passing as a team
topics.focus: moving the ball between football teammates
A: Passing helps football players share the ball.

Working together keeps the ball moving between players.
AA: Passing is one way football players share the ball.

topics.spareAA: A player practises aiming shots at the goal.

topics.title: Choosing a library book

A: A reader looks for clues when choosing a book.

topics.spareAA: A plastic cover protects the book while it is on loan.

topics.spareAA: Paint colours can help a treehouse blend with nearby leaves.
topics.whyA: The roof’s colour concerns appearance, rather than working safely with an adult.
topics.whyAA: Choosing colours changes how the treehouse looks. It does not explain safe working arrangements.

A: A model bridge needs a strong frame.

topics.spareAA: The bridge is painted to match a nearby model village.
topics.whyA: The stars decorate the model, rather than helping to hold it up.
topics.whyAA: Matching paint colours concerns appearance, rather than the parts supporting the crossing.

topics.title: Sharing mixing jobs

topics.spareA: The batter is pale yellow in the bowl.
topics.spareAA: The recipe combines flour, eggs and milk in one mixture.

topics.whyAA: The ingredients describe what is being mixed. The paragraph explains who does each mixing job.

topics.spareAA: A soft case protects the binoculars inside a backpack.
topics.whyA: The footprints describe the walk, rather than how binoculars help the hikers see wildlife.
topics.whyAA: The case protects the binoculars during storage. It does not explain using them to observe from a distance.

topics.title: Making a snowman’s base

A: A large snowball makes a snowman’s base.

AA: A snowman needs a broad base to support its upper parts.

topics.spareAA: A scarf gives the snowman a cheerful winter look.

topics.title: Talking about a shared story

A: Friends can work out a story together.

topics.spareAA: They use a bookmark to save the page for tomorrow.

topics.title: Checking a robot’s connection

A: A loose plug can stop a small robot from working.

topics.spareAA: Different wheel sizes change how the robot moves.

topics.whyAA: Wheel sizes affect movement. The paragraph focuses on tracing an electrical connection problem.

topics.title: Comparing glider landings

A: Glider landings give the flyers results to compare.

topics.spareAA: A shooter bends their knees before aiming at the hoop.

A: A pony’s coat should be brushed gently.

topics.whyAA: A feeding routine is another part of pony care, but it does not explain gentle, supervised brushing.

A: A space model helps children share their ideas.

topics.spareAA: Clear varnish protects the model’s painted surface.
